clue.text: Splits up with model after row kicks off in Norfolk town

indicators.note: the built-up pieces are placed inside the Norfolk town

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, in eastern England

indicators.note: the up-plus-model pair is placed after the row's opening letter
what kicks off the word row is its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: Someone storms off in a small Norfolk town after a row breaks out, taking a model with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Splits up' reads as one phrase, but only 'Splits' is the definition; 'up' is a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean breaks apart or throws into disorder, as a protest disturbs a meeting.

clue.text: After moving his piano, pensioner lost a stone

indicators.note: after shifting signals that one letter of the pensioner is relocated within it

parts.note: OAP is old-age pensioner
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
L is the sporting abbreviation for lost in results tables

explanation.surface: A pensioner shifting a piano sheds a stone in weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost a stone' looks like weight loss; a stone is 14 pounds in British use, but here it is a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: The gem with a milky play of colours is a precious stone.

clue.text: Letting out a little laugh, English drunk sounds like a horse

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling into a new order
letting something out means releasing it, so a letter leaves the word
a little of the word laugh is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A tipsy Englishman's giggle comes out as a whinny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letting out' removes L, the start of 'laugh', from ENGLISH; 'drunk' rearranges the remaining ENGISH.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's characteristic cry is a whinny, so making that call is what the verb describes.

clue.text: Capital's not about to collapse in a state of panic

indicators.note: collapsing letters fall into a new arrangement
not tells us the following abbreviation is left out of the word

parts.note: CA is circa, about
taken as written

explanation.surface: A city's finances are supposedly not on the brink of collapse, amid panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not about' removes CA from CAPITALS; 'to collapse' rearranges the remaining PITALS into TAILSP.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally an aircraft's spiralling dive, figuratively a loss of control and frantic alarm.

clue.text: One finding suitable candidates to lead a horse

parts.note: to head something is to lead it
a hunter is a horse bred for riding to hounds

explanation.surface: Someone sought to take charge of a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A recruiter who seeks out people for senior jobs is described with this term.

clue.text: Setter into being a communist

indicators.note: into puts the setting substance inside the being

parts.note: ens is the philosophical term for an entity or being
gel is something that sets

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler becomes a convert to communism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the compiler, but it is GEL, which sets. ENS is a philosopher's word for being.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Engels co-wrote the Communist Manifesto with Marx.

clue.text: Fool eating soft items from bakery is able to have quickest motion

indicators.note: eating means the fool encloses what follows

parts.note: a nit is a fool
P is piano, soft in music
pies are baked goods

explanation.surface: An idiot scoffing pastries can then run his fastest.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippy describes something that moves quickly and nimbly; the superlative is the fastest.

clue.text: Saw uncontained fire must spread

indicators.note: spread suggests the letters being scattered and reformed
without its container, the word fire loses its outer letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An uncontrolled fire is bound to spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncontained' strips fire to IR; 'spread' mixes IR with MUST. 'Saw' is the noun, an old saying, not the past tense or tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying, a proverb stating something obvious.

clue.text: Getting on a horse, carrying one in case of evacuation

indicators.note: carrying means the horse holds what follows

parts.note: gee-gee is a childish word for a horse, written GG

indicators.note: in places the one within the outer letters
the case of a word is its outer letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Mounting a horse while carrying someone during an evacuation.
explanation.walkthrough: GG is gee-gee, a childish word for a horse; 'carrying' has it hold EIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on in years means growing old, which is what this word describes.

clue.text: An examination of the Golden Boy

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
Al is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A test given to a celebrated young star.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, as in a viva or language exam, is called this.

clue.text: Glutton's first to regret having left porridge

indicators.note: the first of the glutton is the word's opening letter

parts.note: to rue is to regret
L is left

explanation.surface: A greedy eater sorry to have left his porridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin oatmeal porridge, the meal of Oliver Twist's workhouse.

clue.text: The German admitting love for Action Man?

indicators.note: admitting means letting the love in

parts.note: der is German for the
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A German confessing affection for a toy soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: Action Man is a British boy's action figure; here it means a man of action.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who acts rather than talks is a man of action, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Diary-writing MP with get-up-and-go? Yes, after vacation

parts.note: pep means energy or vigour

indicators.note: a vacated word has its inside emptied, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: Is a politician who keeps a diary energetic? Yes, after a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' looks like a holiday but empties YES to YS.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys, the famous diarist who recorded the Great Fire of London, also sat as a Member of Parliament.

clue.text: Most of Pye Corner out of bounds? Cross, I'd go off around current B6

indicators.note: most of the word means all but its final letter
to go off is to explode, scattering these letters around the current that follows
without its bounds the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a cross is shaped like X
I'd is written ID once the apostrophe goes
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Part of a London street corner is off limits, and some cross person reacts to a vitamin.
explanation.walkthrough: Pye Corner in London is where the Great Fire of 1666 stopped, fitting the puzzle's fire theme; 'B6' is the vitamin, not a road or pencil.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitamin B6 is the chemical compound known by this name.

clue.text: Church getting 70% of Last Supper damaged

indicators.note: damaged letters are broken up and rearranged
seventy per cent of ten letters is the first seven

explanation.surface: A church holding a damaged painting of the Last Supper.
explanation.walkthrough: Last Supper has ten letters; 70% keeps LASTSUP, which 'damaged' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral in the City of London, rebuilt by Wren after the Great Fire.

clue.text: Force small boy to leave rejected 21As

indicators.note: to leave means the boy is removed
rejected means turned back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: the answer at 21 across, plural, means sweet courses, also called desserts
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A kid made to leave because he refused his sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: Desserts written backwards is STRESSED; removing ED leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics and engineering, pressure or force applied to a material is called this.

clue.text: Old maid with legs in plaster after leaving behind unending drama

indicators.note: in puts the legs inside the remaining letters
leaving behind means dropping that part from the word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: unending means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a play is a drama
pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: An elderly unmarried woman, legs in plaster, after quitting an endless drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unending' trims PLAY to PLA; 'after leaving behind' drops that from plaster to leave STER.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried woman past the usual age for marriage, an old-fashioned term.

clue.text: One evenly burns in the ads

indicators.note: evenly means taking the letters in even-numbered positions

explanation.surface: One bright idea gets fired up in the advertisements.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the 2nd, 4th, 6th letters and so on of 'burns in the ads'.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined together as a whole, so united and one are equivalent.

clue.text: Taking leading role in Beethoven's Fifth

definitions.meaning: playing the leading part means being in control, commanding
in music the fifth note of a scale has its own name, the one above the subdominant

explanation.walkthrough: 'Beethoven's Fifth' looks like the symphony; it is the fifth degree of the scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruling or in charge, and also the musical name for the fifth degree of a scale.

clue.text: Centres for refugees branded bad for country

indicators.note: centres means the middle letters of each word

explanation.surface: Refugee camps branded unfit for the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Take UG, AND and A, the middles of refugees, branded and bad.
explanation.definitionFit: The East African country on Lake Victoria.

clue.text: Famous street party recalled by writer in New England

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so read backwards

parts.note: the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters

parts.note: the writer is the setter, I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A well-known street party remembered by an author living in New England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New England' looks like the American region; 'New' rearranges ENGLAND with I. The Great Fire of London began in a bakery on this street in 1666.
explanation.definitionFit: The London street where the Great Fire of 1666 began is famous for that reason.

clue.text: Wise broadcast by satellite supporting local therapist

indicators.note: in a down clue the following pieces support, sit below, the pub

parts.note: a local is a pub, PH on maps (public house)

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out, so the word is heard

parts.note: the word said aloud is the plural of the letter Y
Io is a moon of Jupiter

explanation.surface: A smart satellite TV broadcast backing a local therapist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns 'Wise' into the sound of YS.
explanation.definitionFit: A short informal word for a physiotherapist, who treats injuries with exercise and massage.

clue.text: Group of women taking in a hard rock group

indicators.note: taking in means enclosing the a

parts.note: H is hard, as on pencils
R.E.M. was an American rock band

explanation.surface: A group of women welcoming a heavy rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: The women of a Muslim household, or a sultan's wives and concubines.

clue.text: Fruit added to a gruel in president's birthplace

indicators.note: added to puts the fruit first, then the rest joins it

parts.note: a haw is the berry of the hawthorn
gruel stands in for the clue number 11, which in Roman numerals is II

explanation.surface: Fruit stirred into some porridge where the president was born.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue replaces '11' with its answer; read the number as Roman II.
explanation.definitionFit: Barack Obama was born in Honolulu in this US state.

clue.text: Golf course reportedly a beast

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken

parts.note: a links is a seaside golf course

explanation.surface: A wild creature is said to roam a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild cat with tufted ears, so an animal.

clue.text: City such as London is back in strength

indicators.note: back means the letters run backwards

parts.note: a wen is a large crowded city; Cobbett called London the Great Wen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A city like London is regaining its strength.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon, and by extension physical power or vigour.

clue.text: See 21
One coming out of bakery, looking on as fire starts

indicators.note: starts means the opening letters of each word

explanation.surface: A baker watches as the fire takes hold, recalling the Great Fire's bakery origin.
explanation.definitionFit: A baked mass of bread is one item a bakery sells.

clue.text: Can I possibly cover contents in case of fire, as intended?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go in as contents of the outer letters
the case of a word is its outer letters
possibly signals the letters may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Asking if one may insure the contents against fire, as planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intended' looks like a past participle but is a noun, the person one is engaged to.
explanation.definitionFit: One's intended is the person one is engaged to marry.

clue.text: Flyers locally showing one female relative briefly in a state

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside a and the state

parts.note: VA is Virginia
I is one
F is female

indicators.note: briefly means cut short by a letter

parts.note: an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: Flyers in a US state include a woman visiting her aunt.
explanation.definitionFit: The birds of a particular region, so the local flying creatures.
